content:
iOS 27 continues Apple's long-standing trend of giving you more freedom to customise the design of your iPhone lock screen. This year brings a host of new customisation options, wallpaper settings, and other features.

Extended Wallpapers

iOS 27 brings a suite of new Apple Intelligence editing features to the Photos app, including a redesigned Clean Up tool and a Reframe tool. Another new option is Extend, which intelligently expands your images so you can adjust the aspect ratio, fix the horizon, or add more space around the edges.

As shown in the image above, the Extend feature is also making its way to the lock screen in iOS 27. If a photo doesn't match the aspect ratio of your iPhone, or isn't cropped well enough to make a suitable wallpaper, iOS 27 will automatically suggest using Extend to fix it.

Extend uses AI to generate additional content along the edges of an image, giving you more flexibility when setting your iPhone wallpaper.

Custom Wallpapers

iOS 27 brings major improvements to Image Playground, Apple's AI image generation app. The new features in Image Playground will also extend to your iPhone's lock screen. You can now use Image Playground directly within Settings or the wallpaper picker on the lock screen to generate a wallpaper.

Within the wallpaper picker, you'll find a new Image Playground option. This feature creates stylised versions of images from your Photos library, such as "Nostalgic Illustration" and "Animation" styles.

You can also create custom wallpapers from scratch by describing what you want in natural language.

Moving the Clock

iOS 27 finally lets you shrink the clock on your iPhone lock screen. While Apple has let you customise the clock size for years, iOS 27 goes a step further. You can now move the lock screen clock up to the top row of widgets.

This frees up more space on the lock screen so you can see more of your wallpaper. Of course, the trade-off is that it's harder to glance at the time from a distance. However, for many people, the point of the lock screen is to show off your wallpaper, and iOS 27 makes that even easier.

Swiping Away the Now Playing Widget

In iOS 27, you can swipe away the Now Playing widget on your iPhone lock screen. Even if you dismiss the Now Playing widget, whatever you're listening to will keep playing.

If you frequently tap the Now Playing widget on your lock screen by accident, this is a useful addition.

Wrapping Up

iOS 27 is now available to developers and public beta testers. It will launch for all users later this year. What do you think of the new lock screen customisation features in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
